To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the HRM practices are not directly linked to employee performance, (2) the link between the HRM practices and employee performance is mediated by employee commitment and job satisfaction, and (3) the relationship between HRM practices and job satisfaction is mediated by employee involvement and employee participation in organizational decision making.

(a) HRM practices are positively associated with employee attitudes (job satisfaction, organizational commitment and trust in the organization) and employee performance; (b) the relationship between HRM practices and employee attitudes is partially mediated by perceived organizational support (POS); and (c) the relationship between POS and employee performance is partially mediated by employee attitudes.
the high-commitment HR practices have a positive effect on the performance of the organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of high-commitment human resource practices on employee attitudes and behaviors, and their subsequent impact on business performance.
the impact of the employment relationship and high commitment HR practices on employee attitudes, behaviours, and performance.
the relationship between the HRM practices that organizations adopt and the commitment that employees feel towards their employer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high performance work practices are the most important factors that contribute to the success and the performance of the organization.
the relationship between high-commitment human resource management practices and employee attitudes and behaviors is contingent on the nature of the employment relationship.

the high-commitment HRM practices are positively associated with the organizational outcomes such as organizational commitment, job satisfaction, organizational citizenship behaviors, employee retention and organizational performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high performance work systems (HPWS), which are characterized by the use of high commitment HR practices, have been shown to have a positive effect on firm performance.

high commitment HR practices, when implemented with high quality, can lead to a positive work environment, and that this positive work environment can then lead to positive outcomes for employees, such as job satisfaction and organizational commitment, and for the organization, in the forms of employee retention, organizational performance, and financial.
the high-performance work system (HPWS) model has been tested in many different contexts and has been found to have a positive effect on firm performance in most of them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the HR practices of high-commitment management are positively associated with job satisfaction, organizational citizenship behavior, and organizational commitment, while they are negatively associated with job stress.
the HR practices of high-commitment organizations can be replicated in other organizations.
HRM is not only important for employees’ well-being, but it is also important for the well-being of the firm.
